newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says Japan considers easing pork import ban.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says Japan considers easing pork import ban.

text.p: Taiwan Economic Minister Wang Chih-kang said on Wednesday that, after negotiations, Japan was considering easing a ban on imports of Taiwan pork imposed due to an outbreak of hog foot and mouth disease on the island.
"Pork products recommended by Taiwan's Bureau of Commodity Inspection and Quarantine and approved by Japan's authorities can be exported to Japan," Wang told reporters in Taipei.
"Japanese visitors (to Taiwan) could also take pork products back to Japan," he added.

State television said Taiwan officials had held emergency negotiations with Japan after March 20, when Taipei announced the disease outbreak and ordered a temporary ban on all pork exports. Japan banned imports of Taiwan pork a day later.
Wang, interviewed on state television, declined to comment in further detail.
Officials of the cabinet's Council of Agriculture were not available for immediate comment.

A senior council official had told Reuters on Tuesday that it would be "difficult" for Taiwan to resume pork exports to Japan within five years as it would take that long for Taiwan to certify that all feedlots had eradicated the scourge.
Officials have said the Taiwan pork industry's 1996 export value was T$43.6 billion (US$1.55 billion), with Japan alone taking 99 percent.
South Korea began importing Taiwan pork in 1996 but imposed its own ban due to Taiwan's foot and mouth outbreak.

Industry sources said on Wednesday that about 15 percent of Taiwan's 11 million hogs -- or 1.6 million -- were affected by the disease. The farm council has ordered that all hogs at affected farms, even healthy ones, be destroyed.
